Harbor workshop operations review

The Harbor workshop repairs bicycles for local residents. Its spring pilot lasted twelve weeks. The team accepted 240 bicycles, repaired 216, and returned 24 without repair because replacement frames were unavailable. Every accepted bicycle received a numbered receipt. The receipt number stayed with the bicycle through inspection, repair, and collection.

Three mechanics worked Tuesday through Saturday. Volunteers handled reception and collection. The pilot budget was 18000 dollars. Parts cost 7600 dollars, mechanics received 8400 dollars, and the remaining 2000 dollars paid for tools and insurance. No money was spent on advertising. Residents learned about the workshop through the library and community notice boards.

The team recorded turnaround time from acceptance to collection. The median was four days. A long wait for imported brake parts delayed eighteen repairs, although those bicycles were eventually completed. The team decided to keep spare brake cables and common tires in stock. It rejected a proposal to buy a delivery van because the pilot did not establish demand for home collection.

The next pilot will begin in October and run for eight weeks. It will accept at most twenty bicycles each week. The library will keep handling registration. The team will publish weekly counts of accepted, completed, and returned bicycles. The next review will compare turnaround times and parts costs against the spring pilot before deciding whether to expand.
